svg.title: ULTRA-SATISFACTORY
svg.desc: A vaporwave collage banner in the manner of early-2010s album art, for ULTRA-SATISFACTORY, a companion app for the factory game Satisfactory. On a flat hot-pink ground, a white marble bust of a laurel-crowned head in profile stands on a plain block carved VLTRA MMXXVI. At the top right the title ULTRA SATISFACTORY is set in wide-tracked mint capitals over a thin rule, with the Japanese line urutora satisufakutorii (Ultra Satisfactory in katakana) and kojo no tomo (the factory's friend) and a small hexagon-and-cog emblem. A black-and-pink checkerboard floor in perspective creeps toward the viewer in the lower right. A mid-1990s style window titled Ultra-Satisfactory reads: every recipe, building and Space Elevator objective, one click apart. A pointer clicks its three tabs in turn. Objectives: Space Elevator phase 1 of 5, Smart Plating x50, Versatile Framework x100, Automated Wiring x500, click a part for its recipe. Items: find modular frame, 2 per minute from 3 Reinforced Iron Plate + 12 Iron Rod, Assembler, 60 s, 15 MW. Buildings: 477 buildings, 9 do the work, Constructor 4 MW, Assembler 15 MW, Manufacturer 55 MW, click a machine to see what it makes. Its status bar says 140 items, 211 recipes, 477 buildings. A second window, overtime.bmp, shows a small pixel skyline of factory sheds, stacks and one very tall mast over water, fading from sunset to night and back with the lights still on. Late in the loop a dialog called screws.exe opens with a trail of copies: Storage is full of Screws. Make more Screws? The two buttons both say Yes. The pointer presses Yes.
